project.name: Muni-Pal Site Truth & Education Expansion
project.description: Scrub all public EMMA/MSRB references from muni-pal.io, rewrite pages in the Hormozi copy standard, and stand up the education-facility sector (corpus -> benchmarks -> readiness form) with the EMMA system running on the 890.
project.content:
# Muni-Pal Site Truth & Education Expansion

Initiated 2026-08-03 by Stephen (via COS). Three driving ideas:

1. **Eliminate all public EMMA references.** We do not have MSRB/EMMA's permission to reference their brand or attribute our data to them publicly. Internal use of publicly available data retrieval continues; public attribution stops until written approval exists.
2. **Hormozi-style copy.** Pages should read plain and outcome-first: what the visitor gets, why it's credible, what to do next. Less muni jargon. Source library: `MEGA/AREAS/BUSINESS/ACQUISITION` ($100M Offers/Leads/Money Models, Proof Checklist, Branding Playbook).
3. **Education facility sector.** The readiness tooling is over-indexed on healthcare (+ WTE). Add education as a sector — additive, never removing existing sector selection — with categories derived from our own education deals (SVIDA charter-school pipeline) plus EMMA-pulled public deals. Corpus, cost-of-issuance benchmarks, and the knowledge base inform BOTH the new sector AND the constraint plane for what site copy may claim.

## Ground truth (verified 2026-08-03)

- **Canonical repo:** WSL `~/Developer/MUNI-PAL` (GitHub `st3jace/MUNI-PAL`; 890 bare mirror `/c/Users/st3ja/muni-pal.git`). The OneDrive copy is superseded — do not commit there.
- **Deployments:** marketing site = Vercel (project `muni-pal`, `frontend/vercel.json`, three Vite builds: healthcare root, sensing `/tools/`, readiness `/readiness/`); API = Railway `api.muni-pal.io` (env currently unreadable by agents).
- **EMMA/MSRB inventory:** 11 deployed frontend files carry user-visible references (8 React pages + 3 HTML shells), ~31 instances, incl. two internal-crawler leaks in `CreditSpreadMonitor.tsx` empty states ("Run the EMMA crawler..."). Full list embedded in the M1 issues.
- **Sector plumbing:** top-level sector list is data-driven — `src/munipal/services/sensing.py` `_SEED_SECTORS = ["waste", "healthcare"]`, questionnaires from `sensing_seed/questionnaire_{sector}.json`. Education exists only as an unreferenced stub `EDUCATION_PLAYBOOK_CONFIG` (`playbook_data.py` ~:4224) with 6 empty readiness dimensions, plus `education_facilities` keys in `risk_reporting_service.py`.
- **EMMA system relocation:** crawler/PDF corpus must run and live on the 890, not the ST3 laptop (Stephen 2026-08-03). This aligns with Knowledge Plane issues ART-82 (landing-to-890 sweep), ART-83 (catalog regen on 890), ART-84 (EMMA metadata ingestion).
- **Per-token API costs** for corpus synthesis route through Arthur's stack on the 890, not laptop sessions.

## Relationship to other ART projects

- **Muni-Pal Canonical Knowledge Plane** (ART-62..114) owns KB infrastructure: ingestion, policy engine, retrieval, evidence/citation policy (ART-64), corpus expansion side quest (ART-113). This project CONSUMES that plane for the education sector and the copy constraint plane; it does not rebuild it.
- **Muni-Pal Relationship Intelligence Platform** (ART-17..61) — unrelated buildout; do not mix repos (`muni-pal-platform` is a different repo where Arthur has WIP).

## Owners

- Arthur (890): education corpus/taxonomy/benchmarks/questionnaire, claims certification, EMMA permission research.
- Laptop/COS lane: site copy edits, sector wiring, Vercel deploy verification.
- Stephen: final tone approval, sending EMMA/MSRB outreach, Vercel/Railway credentials where agents are blocked.

milestones.title: M0 — Language governance & copy standard
milestones.description: Decide the rules before touching pages: what we may say (EMMA/MSRB policy + replacement lexicon), how we say it (Hormozi copy standard), and the path to eventually saying more (MSRB permission track). Everything in M1/M2 executes against these two documents.

milestones.title: M1 — De-EMMA the public site
milestones.description: Remove every user-visible EMMA/MSRB reference from muni-pal.io — React copy, HTML shell meta/OG/noscript tags, committed dist bundles — and verify zero references on the live site post-deploy. Ships fast and independently of the M2 rewrite. Compliance-driven: we lack permission to use the EMMA name publicly.

milestones.title: M2 — Hormozi-style page rewrites
milestones.description: Rewrite the public pages to the copy standard from M0: outcome-first headlines, plain language, proof we can substantiate, one clear CTA per page. Includes a claims audit so every quantitative statement traces to corpus artifacts we can stand behind WITHOUT EMMA attribution.

milestones.title: M3 — Education facility sector build (890 / Arthur)
milestones.description: Stand up education as a first-class sector: taxonomy from our own deals + EMMA-pulled public data, corpus crawl running ON THE 890 (PDFs never land on the ST3 laptop), COI/spread benchmarks, questionnaire + readiness framework, and additive end-to-end registration so Education appears alongside Healthcare and Waste-to-Energy in the readiness sector picker. Leans on Knowledge Plane ART-82/83/84; per-token API work routes through Arthur.

milestones.title: M4 — Launch & verification
milestones.description: Education readiness live on muni-pal.io, scrubbed + rewritten copy verified in production, carry-forward list recorded.

deliverables.title: EMMA/MSRB reference policy + approved replacement lexicon
deliverables.description:
**Owner: COS drafts, Arthur reviews, Stephen approves.**

Write `docs/marketing/LANGUAGE-POLICY.md` in the MUNI-PAL repo (WSL canonical).

**Policy core:**
- Zero public-facing use of "EMMA" or "MSRB" (names, logos, attribution) on muni-pal.io, exports, PDFs, emails, or marketing until written permission exists (see d-emma-permission-track).
- Internal use of publicly available EMMA data retrieval CONTINUES for KB/corpus building — public data access is not the issue; public brand attribution is.
- Aligns with Knowledge Plane ART-64 (evidence & citation policy) — cite that issue, don't fork the policy.

**Replacement lexicon to codify (draft — finalize in the doc):**
- "866 actual EMMA transactions" -> "866 actual municipal bond transactions" / "866 deals in our municipal bond corpus"
- "the EMMA corpus" -> "our municipal bond corpus"
- "real EMMA data" / "EMMA filings" -> "public municipal disclosure filings" / "observed market data"
- "filed with EMMA" (continuing-disclosure context) -> "filed in the public municipal disclosure system" (check each usage — some describe the ISSUER's obligations and may need different phrasing)
- "MSRB EMMA municipal bond corpus" (ReportExport attribution) -> "our corpus of public municipal disclosure data"
- Empty-state crawler language ("Run the EMMA crawler...") -> visitor-appropriate copy ("Data for this sector is coming soon").

**Also decide and record:** whether transaction counts (866) stay (they can — the number is ours), and the disclaimer posture (current live landing has NO MSRB G-42 advisor disclaimer; the undeployed variant-b/c drafts do — flag to Stephen as a separate legal question, do NOT silently add or remove).

deliverables.title: MSRB/EMMA data-use permission track (workaround now, approval later)
deliverables.description:
**Owner: Arthur (research + draft), Stephen (send/sign).**

We want to eventually reference EMMA openly. Until then we operate on workarounds (generic attribution per d-emma-policy).

**Tasks:**
1. Research MSRB's actual licensing path: EMMA subscription products, commercial data-use agreements, what redistribution/attribution rights each grants, cost, and whether our use (aggregated benchmarks derived from public disclosures, no bulk redistribution) even requires a license vs. merely brand-name permission.
2. Document findings in the MUNI-PAL repo (`docs/marketing/EMMA-PERMISSION-TRACK.md`): what we can already do freely with public data, what requires agreement, recommended ask.
3. Draft the outreach letter/application for Stephen to send.
4. Record status; this issue stays open until approval or a documented decision not to pursue.

**Constraint:** nothing external goes out without Stephen (Arthur is tickets-only / nothing-external).

deliverables.title: Muni-Pal copy standard distilled from the Hormozi library
deliverables.description:
**Owner: COS/laptop lane. Source library:** `C:\Users\st3ja\OneDrive\Documents\MEGA\AREAS\BUSINESS\ACQUISITION` — $100M Offers / Leads / Money Models course transcripts, $100M Branding Playbook, Proof Checklist, ACQ Ads Handbook, Lead Nurture Playbook.

Produce `docs/marketing/COPY-STANDARD.md` in the MUNI-PAL repo: a working standard any page rewrite can be checked against, not a book report.

**Must cover:**
- **Value equation framing** (dream outcome x perceived likelihood / time delay x effort): every page leads with the outcome the CFO/board gets, not the tool's mechanism.
- **Offer clarity:** name what each tool does in plain words ("Know what a bond will cost you before you talk to anyone" beats "COI benchmarking powered by corpus spreads").
- **Proof-first:** use the Proof Checklist — real numbers (866 deals, spread differentials), specificity over adjectives; every proof point must survive the d-claims-audit constraint plane.
- **Jargon policy:** define the allowed technical floor (DSCR, spread, COI need one-line plain-English glosses on first use; internal terms like "corpus", "sensing", "crawler" never appear).
- **One CTA per page** and what it is (free readiness assessment as the lead magnet, per $100M Leads).
- **Page checklist** (10 items max) used as the acceptance test in M2 issues.

deliverables.title: Claims audit — build the constraint plane and certify every public claim
deliverables.description:
**Owner: Arthur certifies (keeper of bond intelligence); COS assembles. Blocked by: d-emma-policy.**

Build the "what we can say vs. what we stay away from" plane that Stephen described, then run every quantitative/empirical claim on the site against it.

**Method:**
1. Extract every claim from current + rewritten copy (866 transactions; AA vs BBB spread differentials; DSCR/payer-mix/days-cash benchmarks; COI figures; "6 readiness dimensions"; etc.).
2. For each: source artifact (corpus DB, benchmarks JSON, playbook), whether it survives no-EMMA attribution, freshness, and known data-quality caveats (e.g., the housing corpus's implausible $3.25B Canyon Ridge principal shows extraction can produce garbage — education corpus will need the same scrutiny before its numbers go public).
3. Output: `docs/marketing/CLAIMS-REGISTER.md` — claim | source | status (approved / rephrase / remove) | owner.
4. Arthur signs off via ticket comment; COS applies removals/rephrases.

This register becomes the standing gate for ALL future site claims, including education benchmarks from M3.

deliverables.title: Education sector taxonomy & archetypes from our deals + public data
deliverables.description:
**Owner: Arthur (890).**

Define the education-facility sector the way housing was defined (archetypes + quotas), seeded from BOTH:
1. **Our own deal experience** — the SVIDA pipeline is charter-school heavy (Paideia 2022/2026, ALA Johnston, Harvest Prep, etc.; see the Deal Pipeline workbook via bond-mirror). Extract the deal-type patterns we have actually closed.
2. **EMMA-pulled public education deals** — categories we can only derive from what's actually in the public record.

**Candidate archetypes to validate (not prescriptive):** charter school revenue bonds; private/independent K-12; higher-ed auxiliary/revenue; student housing (may overlap housing sector — decide the boundary); cultural/education facility conduit deals.

**Deliverables:**
- `emma/emma_core/sectors/education.yaml` sector profile (mirror `housing.yaml` structure) with archetype quotas sized to actual EMMA availability (lesson from housing: 9% LIHTC quota was structurally unfillable — size quotas from a discovery pass, not aspiration).
- Alignment with `docs/development/SECTOR_ARCHETYPES.md` (canonical archetypes, commit 30ebfe5a) and the 6 readiness dimensions already stubbed in `EDUCATION_PLAYBOOK_CONFIG` (issuer_authority, enrollment_demand, financial_operations, facility_capital, accreditation_compliance, security_collateral).
- Short taxonomy memo into the knowledge base for retrieval.

deliverables.title: Education EMMA crawl running on the 890
deliverables.description:
**Owner: Arthur (890). Blocked by: d-edu-taxonomy (needs education.yaml). Depends on Knowledge Plane ART-82 (landing-to-890 sweep) + ART-83 (catalog regen on 890).**

**Hard constraint from Stephen (2026-08-03): the EMMA system runs on the 890. PDFs and corpus artifacts do NOT land on the ST3 laptop.** Historically the housing crawl ran laptop-side (scheduled tasks, C:\Python314 + Playwright user-site); this workstream moves/execs education crawling 890-side.

**Inherit the housing crawl lessons (all verified 2026-07-28, may have moved since):**
- `click_tab` selectors are STALE vs EMMA's current detail-page markup -> all secondary tabs (interest_rate/trade_activity/ratings/disclosures) come back empty, deals score `critical`. Top blocker; needs a live-markup diagnostic before bulk crawling (EMMA gates on a terms click-through — don't run diagnostic concurrent with a crawl).
- `--resume` has never worked at single-pass level (`sector_crawler._run_single_pass()` drops it); every run restarts at item #1 and the corpus caps at `--max-per-pass` per run.
- Timeout fix (bounded networkidle waits) took throughput 36min -> ~3min per deal; keep it.
- Run per-archetype passes — principal-descending queues starve small archetypes.
- Data-quality gate before benchmarks: implausible extracted values (housing had a $3.25B apartment deal) must be quarantined.

**Deliverables:** education crawl operational on the 890 (Playwright env + scheduling — Hermes cron with pinned provider/model per estate rule), first corpus batch landed under the knowledge plane's storage layout, crawl-state runbook committed.

deliverables.title: Education cost-of-issuance + spread benchmarks
deliverables.description:
**Owner: Arthur (890). Blocked by: d-edu-crawl (needs corpus volume).**

Build the education equivalents of the healthcare data plane that powers the public tools:
- COI benchmarks by deal size band and archetype (feeds `CoiBenchmarking` + `BenchmarkCalculator`).
- Observed spread data by rating/archetype (feeds `CreditSpreadMonitor`).
- Readiness benchmark thresholds for the questionnaire scoring (enrollment trends, debt-service coverage, days cash, facility utilization — final set from d-edu-taxonomy dimensions).

**Cost routing per Stephen:** any per-token LLM extraction/synthesis runs through Arthur's stack on the 890 — NOT laptop Claude API calls.

**Quality gates:** benchmarks ship only from deals passing the data-quality quarantine; every published number gets a row in the CLAIMS-REGISTER (d-claims-audit) with its source artifact; until corpus N is adequate, thresholds may be methodology-derived but MUST be labeled as such internally (housing playbook precedent: synth-labeled numbers, never silently presented as observed).

Questions organized under the 6 stubbed readiness dimensions from `EDUCATION_PLAYBOOK_CONFIG`: issuer_authority, enrollment_demand, financial_operations, facility_capital, accreditation_compliance, security_collateral.
2. If taxonomy justifies sub-sectors (e.g., charter vs. higher-ed), follow the healthcare sub-sector pattern (`_HEALTHCARE_SUB_SECTORS` in `sensing.py` :61-86 + per-subsector questionnaire files) — but ship a single education questionnaire first if sub-sector data is thin.
3. Populate `EDUCATION_PLAYBOOK_CONFIG` (playbook_data.py ~:4224) — replace the `0.1.0-stub` with real contributing_paths/critical_paths per dimension.
4. Offline fallback: copy `questionnaire_education.json` into `frontend/public/data/` (and fix the missing waste fallback per d-scrub-leaks while in there).
5. Question WORDING follows the M0 copy standard — plain language, no jargon without gloss (a charter-school CFO should never need a muni glossary to answer).

**Stephen's explicit constraint: do NOT remove the existing readiness sector selection — education is ADDED alongside Healthcare and Waste-to-Energy.**

Note the sector list also derives from `emma/bond_os_extractor/data/*/corpus.db` scan — confirm behavior when the 890-resident corpus isn't on the API host (Railway); the seed list is the guarantee.
2. `src/munipal/services/sector_profiles.py` — add `education` to `_PROFILES` (:189-193) and aliases (`education`, `education_facilities`, `edu`, `schools`) to `_SECTOR_ALIASES` (:198-209).

4. `risk_reporting_service.py` already has `education_facilities` keys (:99, :148, :179, :212) — verify key-name consistency (`education` vs `education_facilities`) across the whole path.
5. Frontend `ReadinessAssess.tsx`: sector picker is API-driven (sectorsQuery :483-489) so education should appear automatically — verify, and add presentation metadata if the picker needs an icon/label entry. Internal `ProjectList.tsx` :46 hardcodes sector options — add education there too.
6. `readinessLocal.ts` `getLocalSectors()` (:125-136) currently returns healthcare only — add education (+ waste) so offline fallback matches.
7. Tests: sector round-trip (list sectors -> questionnaire -> submit) for education; regression: healthcare + waste questionnaires still resolve.

**Acceptance:** /tools/readiness shows Education alongside Healthcare and Waste-to-Energy; full assessment completes with real questions; existing sectors unchanged.

deliverables.title: Launch: education readiness live + full-site verification
deliverables.description:
**Owner: laptop/COS lane + Stephen. Blocked by: d-edu-wire, d-scrub-verify, d-rewrite-landing, d-rewrite-tools.**

1. Deploy backend (Railway — Stephen may need to be hands for env/deploy given agent access is blocked) and frontend (Vercel).
2. End-to-end on production: select Education in /tools/readiness, complete the questionnaire, receive scored results; education benchmarks render where wired (or show the new visitor-appropriate empty states, never crawler language).
3. Re-run the zero-EMMA/MSRB grep on all live routes (regression check on d-scrub-verify).
4. Copy spot-check against the COPY-STANDARD checklist on the live pages.
5. Record carry-forwards (thin-corpus caveats, benchmarks still methodology-derived, permission-track status) in the issue and hand the list to the Knowledge Plane project where relevant.
